PullRequest.Title: Agents - improve multi-file diff editor actions
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request moves the Word Wrap and Diff View actions from the header's "..." menu to the tab row's "..." menu for better accessibility and usability. 

### Changes made:
- **Word Wrap Action**: 
  - Moved for the Changes tab and multi-file diff editors to the tab row's `1_diff` group, alongside the existing Word Wrap for text files.
  
- **Diff View Submenu**: 
  - Relocated for the Changes tab, text diff, and multi-file diff editors to the same group in the tab row, following the Word Wrap action.

- **Context Handling**: 
  - Updated both Word Wrap actions to correctly read their first argument as the editor context, ensuring they reset the temporary wrap state properly.

- **Tests**: 
  - Adjusted tests in `changesViewActions.test.ts` to verify the new locations of the Diff View and Word Wrap actions, ensuring they are no longer present in the header menu.

### Additional Notes:
- The placement of the Collapse/Expand All Diffs actions remains unchanged as they were not specified for relocation.
- The changes improve the visibility of these actions in the tab row, aligning with user expectations for easier access.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added command path, synchronous storage-event fanout, clear/recreate lifecycle, and full-collection traversal are directly traced in repository code. Exact pause duration depends on changed-file count and number of live multi-diff panes, but the repeated O(N) main-thread mechanism is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, tree-model objects, resource-label objects, and DOM/list widget objects for every changed file
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each transition from hidden to shown synchronously reconstructs the file-list widget and calls setChildren over all N diff items; the profile-scoped storage event is shared, so the work is multiplied by each live multi-diff editor pane observing the setting. Repeated Toggle Details invocations repeat that O(N) construction.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Main-thread UI latency and GC pressure when showing the list, potentially producing a visible pause for multi-diffs containing hundreds or thousands of changed files.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: In a Sessions window, Toggle Details only changed the auxiliary detail panel; it did not write the shared multi-diff file-list preference or synchronously rebuild changed-file trees. The existing Toggle Files caller is excluded from Sessions windows.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added branch routes the commonly used Toggle Details command/keybinding through toggleMultiDiffEditorFileList. Its synchronous profile-storage notification causes MultiDiffEditorWithFileListWidget to recreate MultiDiffEditorFileList on show; that constructor immediately maps all diff items (and builds a ResourceTree in tree mode) before setChildren returns.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 643 is the new Sessions-window caller of toggleMultiDiffEditorFileList; the preceding context-match branch did not exist before the PR, so Toggle Details previously followed only that.toggleDetails() and never triggered the shared file-list reconstruction path.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding every changed-file tree on Toggle Details
Findings.Impact: With a large generic multi-diff open in the Sessions editor area, hide the file list and invoke Toggle Details again. The command now blocks while rebuilding the complete file tree; repeating the command repeats the allocation and traversal, and multiple live editor groups react to the same profile event.
Findings.Evidence: The changed call at line 643 writes/removes multiDiffEditor.fileListHidden. observableMultiDiffEditorFileListVisible subscribes to that profile key for every editor. MultiDiffEditorWithFileListWidget's visibility autorun clears its MultiDiffEditorFileList when disabled and createInstance()s a new one when enabled. The new list's constructor derives the full viewModel.items array and synchronously runs getFileListElements(currentItems, ...), then _tree.setChildren(...). getFileListElements maps every item in list mode and additionally creates a ResourceTree/path nodes in tree mode; no item-count cap is present.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the MultiDiffEditorFileList instance while disabled and only toggle the split-view visibility, rebuilding it when the underlying view model or mode actually changes; if releasing the hidden tree is required for memory, defer/chunk creation off the command stack and coalesce repeated visibility changes. Keep the shared persisted visibility semantics and group routing unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update the Sessions tab-row overflow actions while opening or switching text, diff, and multi-diff editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active editor's scoped context keys are evaluated and the already-registered menu actions are grouped for the tab-row toolbar. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached; submenu contents are instantiated from in-process registrations.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Menu/action count and context-expression key count; the diff adds a constant number of actions and constant-size expressions, independent of changed-file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread menu refresh per editor/context change; menu change events are in-process and no asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu registrations are process-lifetime objects. Warm editor switches reuse the registrations and only reevaluate context keys; there is no cold/warm external cache distinction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed registrations and the editor toolbar's createEditorActions path were inspected, and no expensive boundary or scaling loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Toolbar implementation costs depend on total contributed actions, but this PR adds only constant work and moves two existing entries rather than adding collection-scaled rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: moving Word Wrap and Diff View between in-process menus adds only constant context evaluation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Word Wrap from the Sessions tab-row overflow for a text or multi-diff editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command scans its small argument tuple, resolves the targeted editor group, performs one existing configuration update, then clears transient wrap state for at most the original and modified code editors. The awaited configuration update remains the only external persistence work on the command path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the sessions.editor.wordWrap or sessions.diffEditor.wordWrap configuration value, ultimately persisting configuration through the existing configuration service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one configuration update per user invocation; not per file or diff row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff the same action performed exactly one awaited configuration update; only editor-command context extraction changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action awaits this existing update before completing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the action argument count and two code-editor models; neither scales with the number of files in a multi-diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serialized awaited configuration write per click; no new parallelism, queue, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observable word-wrap settings reflect configuration changes; no changed cache key, invalidation, or miss behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed handler and transitive options-service setters were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying configuration persistence latency varies by host, but its count and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: args.find(isEditorCommandsContext) is constant over the tiny command tuple and preserves the existing single persistence operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use Toggle Details on a multi-diff editor with the experimental changed-files list in a Sessions window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new branch synchronously evaluates the editor-group context, writes/removes one profile storage key, and synchronously notifies every live observer. On a show transition each observing widget constructs a new changed-file list and performs a full setChildren traversal before the command stack completes; durable storage flushing is deferred and is not the dominant critical-path cost.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and write/remove the profile-scoped multiDiffEditor.fileListHidden storage value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read plus one store/remove per Toggle Details invocation; the resulting in-process event fans out to each live multi-diff editor pane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Toggle Details in Sessions only toggled the auxiliary detail panel and did not touch the multi-diff profile key or notify file-list observers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The in-memory storage mutation and observer delivery are synchronous; backing-store flush is deferred, but observer-triggered tree reconstruction blocks the UI command.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N changed files in each live multi-diff view model, multiplied by G live editor panes observing the shared profile key; every hide/show cycle repeats the O(N*G) construction on show.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread fan-out through the shared storage event; there is no limiter, deferral, coalescing, or background construction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The hidden transition clears and disposes the list. Therefore the next show is a cold reconstruction even when the view model and files are unchanged; there is no reusable warm tree.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added caller, shared observable, clear/create autorun, full item mapping/ResourceTree build, and synchronous setChildren call were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact pause duration depends on file count, path depth, and live editor-group count, but the full-collection synchronous reconstruction and repeated cold lifecycle are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity synchronous UI regression; submitted as a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Files View & Position submenu in Sessions and switch list/tree mode or left/right position
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the submenu evaluates constant context keys. Selecting a mode or position performs one existing profile-storage update; a mode change then rebuilds the active list representation over its changed files, while position changes move the existing split-view child.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store/remove the shared file-list view-mode or position preference in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage mutation per explicit selection, shared across live multi-diff panes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These commands and their storage behavior existed, but their submenu was excluded from Sessions; the PR exposes the same actions there.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: In-memory observer notification is synchronous; persistence flush is deferred. Tree/list mode selection necessarily recomputes the selected representation, while position reuses the existing list.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Opening the menu is constant. An explicit view-mode switch scales with N changed files per live pane; a position switch is constant aside from split-view relayout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous shared-state fan-out, with no asynchronous boundary burst. Operations occur only on explicit user selections.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Position changes retain the existing list. View-mode changes reuse the widget but rebuild the representation because the grouping semantics changed; no external cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: action preconditions, storage setters, and list autorun were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large diffs can make a mode switch noticeable, but it is a one-time representation change explicitly requested by the user rather than avoidable repeated work introduced by menu placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the newly exposed mode operation's O(N) rebuild is required to change representation, and position changes preserve the list.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open accessibility help while focus is in the multi-diff changed-files list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider validates the active editor, reads the in-process environment flag, localizes four strings, and creates an AccessibleContentProvider. No external operation must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed four-string content array, independent of changed-file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous provider creation on explicit help invocation; no queued or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted or changed; the additional Sessions/non-Sessions branch is a constant environment read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete provider method was inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; content size is fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added environment lookup and alternate localized string are constant-time and off normal rendering/input paths.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 10 changed files. One medium-severity finding was submitted for the newly routed Toggle Details command synchronously recreating full changed-file trees through shared storage fan-out; other menu, word-wrap, submenu, and accessibility changes add only constant work or retain existing boundary counts.
